title: Al-Inshiqaq 84:11-15 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Inshiqaq and the sifat of strength
source: Written for quran/y6 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Inshiqaq 84:11-15 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 12. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: فَسَوْفَ يَدْعُوا۟ ثُبُورًۭا (١١) وَيَصْلَىٰ سَعِيرًا (١٢) إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ فِىٓ أَهْلِهِۦ مَسْرُورًا (١٣) إِنَّهُۥ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ (١٤) بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًۭا (١٥)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: He will cry out for destruction
And [enter to] burn in a Blaze.
Indeed, he had [once] been among his people in happiness;
Indeed, he had thought he would never return [to Allah].
But yes! Indeed, his Lord was ever of him, Seeing.

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Inshiqaq 84:11-15 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 84:11-15 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 84:11-15 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Write what 'his Lord was always seeing him' means for how we behave when alone.
questions.a: We behave well even when no one is watching, because Allah sees us.

questions.q: In 84:14 find two different idgham next to each other and explain them.
questions.a: أَن لَّن: noon into laam, no hum; لَّن يَحُورَ: noon into yaa, with hum.
A) always seeing him. 'Indeed, his Lord was ever, of him, Seeing' (84:15).

questions.q: Al-Inshiqaq 84:13: «إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Someone is happy and careless now, sure he will never return to Allah. What is he forgetting?
questions.a: That his Lord was always seeing him (84:15). Being joyful is fine; forgetting Allah is the problem (84:13 to 14).
